research_mode: official ONS, Home Office National Data Library and Police.uk web sources only; LSOA denominator, population methodology, survey weighting, record-revision, availability, identifier and approximate-location guards; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Lower layer Super Output Area population estimates
verified_claims: released 7 November 2025
provides mid-year usual-resident population estimates for LSOAs in England and Wales by broad age groups and sex
the current listed edition covers revised mid-2022 through mid-2024
limitations: an LSOA population denominator is not a parcel population
edition and geography year must match the crime and boundary evidence before calculating any rate

sources.name: Population estimates by output areas, electoral, health and other geographies QMI
verified_claims: last revised 7 November 2025
small-area population products have different statistical designations depending on geography and age disaggregation
SAPE is the official source of between-census population estimates for Super Output Areas and other listed geographies
limitations: accredited, in-development and supporting-information products must not be treated as equivalent
the QMI establishes methodology and suitability rather than a target-parcel result

sources.name: SAPE rebased backseries and correction notice
verified_claims: mid-2012 to mid-2020 estimates were rebased onto Census 2021 LSOA and MSOA geographies
a faulty OA lookup was corrected on 12 March 2025
the documented lookup error did not affect the accredited LSOA, MSOA or health-geography statistics
limitations: correction impact varies by geography and must not be generalised across products
superseded OA-derived files must not be silently combined with corrected editions

sources.name: Methodology for production of small-area population estimates
verified_claims: SOA estimates use a ratio-change methodology based on changes in administrative population sources
LSOA estimates are constrained to MSOA estimates and MSOA estimates to local-authority estimates
from mid-2021 onwards the Personal Demographics Service is the administrative change source used for SOA estimates
limitations: modelled and constrained population estimates are not direct enumerations of each parcel
special-population and usual-residence definitions must be preserved when interpreting denominators

sources.name: Lower layer Super Output Area population density
verified_claims: released 7 November 2025
provides LSOA population density based on usual-resident mid-year estimates
the current listed edition covers revised mid-2022 through mid-2024
limitations: population density is contextual exposure information rather than a crime or safety outcome
density must not be converted into a parcel safety score without a preregistered and validated method

sources.name: User guide to crime statistics for England and Wales: March 2026
verified_claims: CSEW is a household victimisation survey covering experiences in the 12 months before interview
for covered crimes it better reflects unreported crime and long-term trends than police recorded crime
its primary purpose is national estimates with only some headline figures available regionally
limitations: national and regional survey estimates cannot be assigned to an LSOA or parcel
domestic and sexual violence in interviewer-led sections are subject to under-reporting and preferred self-completion measures are separate

sources.name: CSEW weighting, denominator and suppression conventions
verified_claims: CSEW incidence counts use population or household denominators while prevalence represents the percentage of adults or households victimised
population estimates must match the same subpopulation used by the survey table
weights adjust for differential non-response and published conventions suppress low-base or disclosure-sensitive cells
limitations: national survey weighting does not create small-area representativeness
incidence, prevalence, household and personal denominators must not be interchanged

sources.name: Police recorded crime: transferred or cancelled records
verified_claims: published by the Home Office and last updated 8 July 2026
records may later be transferred or cancelled when a crime was recorded in error or verifiable information shows that no crime occurred
the circumstances are governed by Home Office Crime Recording Rules
limitations: an initially recorded count is not necessarily final
area-level transferred or cancelled totals do not identify which anonymised street record changed

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police API availability contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns the year and month of available street-level crime datasets
each month separately lists force identifiers that supplied stop-and-search data
dates use ISO year-month format
limitations: street-crime month availability does not prove uniform force completeness
stop-and-search availability is force-specific and must not be inferred from the crime month alone

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Outcomes for a specific crime API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns dated outcome history for a specified crime
persistent_id is a 64-character identifier intended to persist while the ordinary API id is not guaranteed to remain stable
the returned street and coordinates are approximate
limitations: the persistent identifier does not convert an approximate map point into an exact incident address
outcomes are unavailable for the Police Service of Northern Ireland and geographic coverage must remain explicit

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Street-level outcomes API contract
verified_claims: street-level outcomes can be queried by location identifier, latitude and longitude, or polygon for a specified month
returned crime locations and street names are approximate
the response can include a status-update-unavailable outcome category
limitations: point or polygon outcome queries are area-context queries rather than parcel observations
missing status updates must not be interpreted as no outcome or no crime

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Crimes at a location API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns crime records at an approximate published location
outcome_status contains the category and date of the latest recorded outcome rather than the full history
the ordinary crime id relates only to the API and is not a police identifier
limitations: latest outcome status must not be mistaken for complete case history
an approximate location and API identifier cannot establish exact target-parcel attribution
